Plantoir 1.8.5

Plantoir 1.8.5 is for the Mac. Windows: no changes — the Windows download stays at 1.7.2 on plantoir.app until it catches up.

Fixed

  • On a first visit to a long page over a slow connection, the text no longer jumps down as each picture arrives. Every picture's size is now written into the page when the site is built, so the browser keeps the right space for it before it has loaded. This finishes the Safari scrolling fix from 1.8.4, and it applies to every browser. A picture you gave a size yourself in your notes is drawn exactly as before. Republish a site to get it.

Plantoir 1.8.4

Plantoir 1.8.4 is for the Mac. Windows: no changes — the Windows download stays at 1.7.2 on plantoir.app until it catches up.

Improved

  • Publishing a class no longer lists curriculum expectation pages as "already visible". They were never going to change, and on a class that cites several expectations they pushed the pages you actually need to read further down the list.
  • The Start of Year sheet shows the pages it will put into draft as a table — page, folder and why — the same way Publish Pages does, with the warnings you need to read before Go kept in view.

Fixed

  • In Safari, scrolling a long page with pictures no longer makes the text jump as each picture arrives. Pictures are now laid out at their full height before they scroll into view. (A very slow first visit can still shift a little until the next release.)

Plantoir 1.8.3

Plantoir 1.8.3 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later on the Mac will offer this update by itself.

Before you update

  • Deploy each section again to get these changes on your sites. A site keeps working exactly as it did until you deploy it with 1.8.3; the app itself looks and works as it did in 1.8.2.

Improved

  • My Progress looks like the entries beside it in the sidebar. It used to show in grey, like a page; it now looks just like All Classes above it.
  • Each page on My Progress opens to show its checklist. Click the arrow beside a unit, a class or a page to see the items under it, each marked ticked or not and linking to that spot on the page; Option-click opens or closes everything inside at once, as in the Finder. The page remembers what was left open.

Fixed

  • A link to a heading lands on that heading. In Safari and Arc, a link to a heading further down a page with runnable code, diagrams or pictures above it could stop well short of the heading. It now lands on it in every browser.

Plantoir 1.8.2

Plantoir 1.8.2 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later on the Mac will offer this update by itself.

Before you update

  • Deploy each section again to bring diagrams back. Since late August, a site deployed to Netlify has shown each Mermaid diagram as the text it was written in, instead of drawing it. Deploying each section again with 1.8.2 draws them all again. Sites on Cloudflare or deployed to a folder were never affected, and neither was Preview.
  • Deploy each section again to get My Progress. A section gains its My Progress page the next time you deploy it with 1.8.2; until then your site keeps working exactly as it did.
  • The app itself looks and works as it did in 1.8.1; what is new reaches your sites and the notes Plantoir keeps for Claude and Codex. If you once said "Not now" to Plantoir's notes for Claude and Codex in your working folder, Plantoir offers them again once, because their words changed.

New

  • My Progress, a page for each student's own progress. When a page in a section has a checklist under a heading named "Test of success", "Tests of success" or "Success criteria", the section's site gains a My Progress page, listed right after the class folder in the sidebar and first in the site's Key Links. It lists each of those pages with how many of its items the student has ticked (for example 3 / 4) and a link back to the page, grouped by the class that first linked it. The ticks are kept in the student's own browser: they are never sent anywhere and you never see them. Course Settings will offer a switch and your own heading names in a later release.
  • Claude Code and Codex know every way a page can be written. When you ask them to revise a course, they read one guide covering callouts, diagrams, tables, maths, checklists, My Progress, links, pictures, videos and more, and it sends them on to the guides for printing, graphs, quizzes and runnable code.

Fixed

  • Mermaid diagrams draw again on sites deployed to Netlify. The rule that keeps Netlify's advertisement badge off your pages was also stopping the diagrams from drawing. See "Before you update".
  • No site loads a page-view counter nobody set up. The site-building tool Plantoir uses came with a page-view counter switched on, though nobody had set one up. It is now switched off on every site and in Preview.

Plantoir 1.8.1

Plantoir 1.8.1 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later on the Mac will offer this update by itself.

Before you update

  • Preview and deploy each section again to bring the new features to your sites. A site deployed by 1.8.0 keeps working exactly as it did. Programs that ask for input as they run, the coloured editor with line numbers, and checklists students can tick reach a site the next time you preview and deploy it with 1.8.1.
  • Programs that ask for input as they run need Netlify or Cloudflare. On a site deployed to a folder or a school web space, students still type their input into the box before pressing Run, as in 1.8.0. So does a page that also shows a video, a PDF or a picture from another website; Plantoir names those pages when you preview and deploy.
  • Code looks a little different on every site. The runnable editor now shows line numbers and your site's colours, every code block has a thin line beside its line numbers, and programming ligatures (where characters such as -> or != are drawn joined as one symbol) are turned off in all code, including code inside a sentence.
  • Checklists on your class sites become tickable. Each student's ticks are kept in their own browser only: they are never sent anywhere, you never see them, and they do not follow a student to another device. Your notes are never changed.
  • The ready-made courses' "What This Site Can Do" pages are rewritten, because they said checklists could not be ticked. If you already created a course from a ready-made one, your copy stays exactly as it is.
  • A course with a colon in its name that you started empty may not build. If its name holds a colon followed by a space (for example "Physics: Mechanics") and you started it with no example content or ready-made pages, the build may say a section's front page cannot be read, near line 2. To fix it, open sectionN/index.md in Obsidian and put double quotes around the title on line 2, so it reads title: "Grade 12 Physics: Mechanics, Section 1". Courses made from now on are written that way already.

Three choices made for now

These are this release's defaults, and a later release may change them:

  • A printed page shows the student's own ticks. When a student prints a page with a checklist, the boxes they ticked print ticked and the others print empty.
  • A fill-in-the-blank question with one blank says "Not quite. Try again, or show the answer." when the answer is wrong, the same as a short-answer question. A question with two or more blanks where exactly one is right says "1 of 2 blanks is right. Try again, or show the answer."
  • Checklist boxes are drawn in dark grey with no fill, and a ticked item's words stay easy to read.

New

  • Programs that stop and ask. In Preview, and on a site deployed to Netlify or Cloudflare, a runnable Python or Swift program now waits when it asks for input: its question appears in the output with a box right after it, and the student types an answer and presses Return, as in a real terminal. Pasting several lines answers one question per line, and "No more input" ends the input.
  • Students can tick the checklists on your pages, and each student's ticks are remembered in their own browser from one visit to the next.
  • plantoir.app has a new Quizzes page showing self-check quizzes in mathematics, chemistry, English and computer science, as assessment as learning.

Improved

  • The runnable editor keeps your site's colours while students type, and every runnable program shows line numbers. A program a student has changed prints in colour, with its line numbers.
  • Fill-in-the-blank feedback reads properly when a question has one blank, rather than "0 of 1 blanks are right" (see "Three choices made for now").
  • Plantoir's offer to add Obsidian's add-ons no longer says Obsidian will open its settings after you trust the author. It does not: the open note simply redraws with its diagrams and graphs.

Fixed

  • A course name with a colon (for example "Physics: Mechanics") no longer stops a section's front page from being built. See "Before you update" for a course you already made.
  • A % sign in the name of a curriculum page no longer stops the site from building, and the coverage map now links pages whose names hold %, # or & correctly. A curriculum folder whose name holds an & no longer appears in the "When did we do this?" lists.
  • Folder pages show their table of contents when they have headings, including your curriculum folder's front page, which ignored "enableToc: true".

Plantoir 1.8.0

Plantoir 1.8.0 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later on the Mac will offer this update by itself.

Before you update

  • Swift programs need a large one-time download. The first time you preview a course that has a Swift program in it, your Mac downloads about 1.3 GB to get Swift ready, and needs about 6 GB of free disk space while it does. This happens once, and only if you use Swift. If there is not enough room, Plantoir says so and the rest of the page builds as usual.
  • Obsidian will ask whether you trust the author. When Plantoir offers to add Obsidian's add-ons for diagrams and graphs and you say yes, Obsidian asks, the first time each course opens with them, whether you trust the author of its pages — that is you. Click "Trust author and enable plugins". Pressing Return chooses the other button, and the drawings then stay as text.
  • Rebuild and deploy your printable sites. On a site built by 1.7.2, Print could stop after "Preparing to print…" in Safari on a printable page you reached by clicking a link from the home page. Preview and deploy each section once with 1.8.0 to fix this.
  • The ready-made ICS3U course has changed. If you already created an ICS3U course from it, your copy stays exactly as it is; the new version, with programs students can run, is what you get when you create an ICS3U course from it after updating.

New

  • Python programs students can run on the page. Add one line to a page's settings and the word "run" to a Python code block, and students get the program in an editor with Run, Stop and Reset. They can change it, type input for it, and see what it prints or the error it hit — in their own browser, with nothing to install and no account.
  • Swift programs too. A Swift code block marked "run" lets students run your program with the input they type. The code itself stays as you wrote it, and Plantoir gets each program ready when you preview the section.
  • Self-check quizzes. Write multiple choice, select all that apply, short answer and fill-in-the-blank questions right in your notes, and students check their own answers on the site, with your explanation once they have. Questions can include maths, graphs, diagrams and programs to run. It is practice, never a grade: nothing a student does leaves their browser.
  • Obsidian shows your diagrams and graphs too. When a course has diagrams or graphs, Plantoir offers once, when you open it in Obsidian, to add the Obsidian add-ons that draw them, so you see the same pictures while you write. Your answer applies to every course that has them, and Plantoir never changes add-ons you installed yourself.
  • Claude Code and Codex know the new features. When you revise a course with them, they know how to make an example runnable or add a short self-check quiz.

Improved

  • The ready-made ICS3U course uses runnable Python throughout: most of its programs can now be run and changed by students right on the page.
  • Maths on your class sites no longer depends on another website. Your own site now serves what it needs to show maths. Your sites pick this up the next time you preview or deploy.
  • Curriculum pages: each overall expectation now lists "When did we do this?", with every class that worked on it or on any of its specific expectations — as the specific expectations already did.
  • Plantoir's activity record (used in problem reports) now shows the full version number when Plantoir opens, and says when and why it closed.
  • plantoir.app has a new Code page showing runnable Python and Swift programs and self-check quizzes.

Fixed

  • A folder you add to an existing course in Course Settings now appears on the site, with its own page in the sidebar and a page to copy, just like a folder made with the course. Folder names with a colon or an ampersand work too.
  • Undo can finish a change it could only partly undo. Once you have dealt with the page you had edited since, pressing Undo again now takes the change off the list instead of getting stuck. The start-of-year undo works the same way.
  • When you make room for classes and other classes have to move, the card's warning that Undo will not take that back is now checked the same way on the Mac and on Windows.

Plantoir 1.7.2

Plantoir 1.7.2 is for the Mac. Windows: no changes — the Windows download stays at 1.7.1, and Windows gets these in a later release. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later on the Mac will offer this update by itself.

New

  • Publish Pages…, Hide Pages… and Publish Class for a Date… in the Section menu now show the pages in a table — each page, its folder and what will happen to it — with a one-line summary above. Every page is listed, the table scrolls, and you can sort it by any column. Press Return to go ahead or Escape to cancel, as before.
  • On your class sites, each page inside an open folder of "Navigate this site" has a small dot before it, and a long title that wraps onto a second line now lines up under its first letter, so it no longer looks like two pages. Your sites pick this up the next time you preview or deploy.

Improved

  • Schedule a deploy no longer asks you to keep a laptop plugged in. It says what matters: the Mac must be on and awake, and on battery it goes to sleep sooner, so keep it awake until then.
  • When a deploy to Cloudflare Pages needs your Account ID, Plantoir now says where to add it: Plantoir ▸ Settings ▸ Deploying.

Fixed

  • Course Settings ▸ Printing showed an empty top-right corner for some courses whose printed handouts carry Name and Date. The sketch now matches the paper.
  • After publishing or hiding pages, the assistant said it had changed your preview even when the rebuild had stopped to ask a question or had not run. It now says the preview changed only when it did.
  • Re-date Classes… that stops part way no longer reports "Nothing was changed": it names the pages that were already re-dated.
  • Plantoir's activity record (used in problem reports) said "changed nothing" after a Make Room for Classes, a partial undo, or a publish that stopped part way, when files had been written. It now says what happened.

Plantoir 1.7.1

Plantoir 1.7.1 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later will offer this update by itself.

Nothing changes unless you ask for it: Preview still opens at your site's front page, exactly as before.

New

  • Preview can pick up where you left off. In Plantoir ▸ Settings ▸ Preview, choose whether pressing Preview opens your site's front page or the page you were last reading in that section's preview.
  • Hold Option to get the other choice for one press — on the Preview button, or with ⌥⇧⌘P from the Section menu.
  • The Preview button and Section ▸ Preview always say what will happen: "Preview" opens the front page, "Preview at Last Viewed" opens the page you left off on. Their names change while you hold Option.
  • Plantoir remembers the last page for each section separately, even after you quit and open it again.
  • If the page you were last reading no longer exists — you renamed or removed it — the preview opens at the front page instead.

Plantoir 1.7.0

Plantoir 1.7.0 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later will offer this update by itself.

Nothing you have already built looks any different on screen. A page without a diagram or a graph shows exactly as it did before, a printable page's handout prints exactly as it did in 1.6.0, and every site you have already deployed stays as it is until you deploy it again.

New

  • Draw a diagram right in your notes with TikZ, the drawing language of LaTeX. Plantoir draws it when the site is built, so students see a crisp picture that follows the site's light or dark theme.
  • Add a graph of a function with a few lines of text. Students can drag it and zoom in, right on the page.
  • Diagrams and graphs print whole, in black on white, from a handout or from the browser's own Print command, even when the page is shown in dark mode.
  • If a diagram or graph can't be drawn, students see one plain sentence in its place, and Plantoir tells you which page, which figure and which line to look at.
  • Claude and Codex know how to add diagrams and graphs to a page. Plantoir writes the guidance into your working folder, so you can ask for "a graph of y = 3(x − 2)² − 4 beside its parent" and get one that works.
  • The ready-made Grade 10 mathematics course (MPM2D) now draws its similar triangles and its parabolas, and its Similar Triangles Practice prints as a handout.

Fixed

  • Printing a page that isn't marked printable, with ⌘P, now prints the whole article. Before, the site's folder list could print over part of the page and hide the words underneath, and in Safari the page could run off the edge of the paper.

To see a diagram inside Obsidian while you write, install Obsidian's TikZJax plugin. Graphs show as text in Obsidian and are drawn when you preview.

Plantoir 1.6.0

Plantoir 1.6.0 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later will offer this update by itself.

Nothing you have already built changes. A page prints as a handout only when you mark it printable; every other page builds exactly as it did before, down to the last byte, and every site you have already deployed stays as it is.

New

  • A page can print as a proper handout. Add printable: true to the settings at the top of a worksheet, review or practice page, and it gains a Print button beside its date.
  • Print offers three choices: Questions only, Answers only, or Both, with the answers starting on a fresh page and numbered separately. Nothing prints until you choose one, and you can choose Portrait or Landscape paper first.
  • The handout looks like a typical typeset worksheet: Latin Modern type, a bold title, questions numbered in the margin with lettered parts set side by side, and a footer with the page's title, the course code and the page number.
  • Answers you write in folded callouts move to the answer key, labelled by the question they belong to. Hints print in place, unfolded.
  • Course Settings has a Printing section: your school's name, the blanks students fill in (Name, Date, Class #), and where the school name and course code print on each page.
  • A page can hand out a PDF you already have instead. Name the file, kept in the course's Media folder, in the page's settings, and Print opens that PDF.
  • Claude, Codex and other assistants are told how to write a page that prints well. Plantoir writes a short guide into your working folder, and if you already keep your own CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md there, it asks before adding a section to the end, leaving your own words untouched.

Improved

  • Pressing Print in Plantoir's own preview opens the page in your web browser, ready to print.
  • On paper, a handout leaves out buttons, menus and the "click to expand" hints, prints diagrams and pictures whole and in light colours, and prints code in a plain box with line numbers.
  • A worked example keeps its box on paper; nothing else is boxed or shaded.
  • A page's Curriculum connections section never prints, in a handout or from the browser's own Print command, so students see the questions rather than the planning.
  • If any part of a handout would be cut off at the edge of the paper, Plantoir says so and prints nothing, rather than handing you a sheet with words missing.

Plantoir 1.5.0

Plantoir 1.5.0 is for the Mac. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later will offer this update by itself.

New

  • A Course menu and a Section menu in the menu bar hold everything you can do to the course or section you have selected, with keyboard shortcuts shown beside them.
  • Things you used to ask the assistant for are now in the Section menu too: Publish Pages…, Hide Pages…, Publish Class for a Date…, Rebuild Preview, Undo Last Change, Add Next Class, Re-date Classes…, Make Room for Classes… and Class Dates…. Each shows you what it will do before it does it. Right-click a section for the everyday ones.
  • When you deploy, Plantoir asks about class pages students can already see that are dated after your next class. You can hide the ones you tick, or keep them all; tomorrow's class, published the evening before, is never asked about.
  • File ▸ Open Recent lists the working folders you have opened, and it and Open Working Folder… work even when no window is open.
  • Help ▸ Publishing and Deploying… explains the difference between the two, and Help ▸ Plantoir Help opens plantoir.app.
  • Plantoir ▸ Settings has a Deploying tab, which holds your Cloudflare Account ID in one place. Course settings and the New Course panel show it, with an Open Settings… button to change it.

Improved

  • Plantoir follows the Mac's own conventions more closely. Escape closes every sheet, Return presses a sheet's main button only when that button can be used, every sheet's title is the same size and shape, and every text field wears the same border.
  • The Delete key removes the course, section, backup or archive you have selected (after asking), and Remove… now sits at the bottom of each right-click menu.
  • Right-clicking a course or section offers Revise With ▸ Claude…, Codex… or Local AI Assistant…, named the same way as in the menu bar.
  • All Backups can be sorted by course, date made or size, and its rows have a right-click menu.
  • When a backup, restore or deletion goes wrong, the message names what could not be done.

Fixed

  • A failed build is no longer blamed on Netlify limiting deploys just because the number 429 appeared somewhere in its output.
  • The − button under the sidebar can no longer remove a section of a course you keep for reference.
  • Copy a Page can now be closed with Escape.

Plantoir 1.4.5

Plantoir 1.4.5 is for the Mac and for Windows. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later will offer this update by itself.

Improved

  • The first window after an update used to be held back while Plantoir got your folder ready — about two minutes on Windows, a few seconds on a Mac. Now the window appears at once, with a notice that says the folder is being got ready and that Preview and Deploy wait for it. Preview and Deploy are available again the moment it finishes: usually a few seconds on a Mac, 15 to 20 seconds on a typical Windows laptop, and longer on a slow disk.
  • Every text field in Plantoir is now the same height and wears the same border: the New Course panel's fields and the Copy a Page search field matched an older look and were two points shorter than the rest.

Fixed

  • When Claude or Codex rebuilds a preview or publishes a page while that section is being deployed, the answer now says the section is being deployed, so the preview cannot be built until that finishes. Before, it only said the preview could not be built. On a Mac the answer also no longer sends you to "that section's window" when Claude or Codex has no window to look in.
  • An update Plantoir found but could not show at the time — because you kept Plantoir in front all day, or had switched away and quit before coming back — is offered again later the same day, and looked for again the next time Plantoir opens, instead of waiting for tomorrow's check.
  • When Claude or Codex schedules a deploy and names classes like "Unit 2, Day 3", the title is no longer cut in half. Class titles are now separated by semicolons, so a comma inside a title stays where you put it.

Plantoir 1.4.4

Plantoir 1.4.4 is for the Mac. Windows: no changes in this release; the Windows download stays at 1.4.3. Plantoir 1.4.0 or later on a Mac will offer this update by itself.

New

  • Plantoir now says "deploy" for putting your website online and "publish" only for marking a page to be included. The words are kept apart everywhere you read them: in the app, in what the assistant says, in the starter pages a new course comes with, and on plantoir.app, where the Publishing page is now called Deploying (the old address still works).
  • Type "schedule a deploy for tomorrow at 6:30 am" to the assistant and it sets that up for you to agree to; "schedule a deploy" with no time asks you for one and never deploys right away; "cancel that scheduled deploy" cancels it. A request that names a later time is never carried out straight away.
  • "Start a new unit with the next class" and "Add three more days to Unit 2" are answered by the assistant exactly as you say them. A request it cannot be sure about is pointed at the wording that does it, rather than adding a page you did not ask for.
  • A Claude or Codex session opened from Plantoir now keeps hold of the course it was opened from, the way the built-in assistant does: its backup is kept, a second session on the same course is refused, and renaming or restoring the course waits until the session ends.

Improved

  • A deploy no longer starts while that section's scheduled deploy is still working, including one left running after Plantoir was closed. The new deploy waits for it, up to thirty minutes, and tells you if it had to stand down.
  • A scheduled deploy's notification now reads "deployed on its own to …", and says that your website has the new pages.
  • The About window and the plantoir.app card say "Grow a class website."

Fixed

  • The "_DUPLICATE ME" page a new course comes with names its heading marks again: "Every ## (level 2) and ### (level 3) heading…". Courses made before this update keep the page as it was.

Plantoir 1.4.3

This release is for the Mac. The Windows download on plantoir.app remains version 1.4.2 for now. On a Mac, Plantoir 1.4.0 or later will offer this update by itself.

New

  • (Mac) Claude and Codex can change a course while its preview is open. They are asked to wait only while Plantoir is actually building that course's website, for a preview or for a deploy. A change made while a preview is open is saved straight away; press Stop Preview, then Preview, to see it.
  • (Mac) Ask Claude or Codex to deploy a section and the deploy goes ahead even when a preview is open. If that closes the preview, Plantoir says "Closed for a deploy" instead of telling you something went wrong.
  • (Mac) Type "publish unit 4, day 3" to the assistant and it is answered straight away.

Improved

  • When two pages have the same name, asking the assistant to publish one now asks which you meant, naming each with its folder.
  • When making room for extra classes cannot finish every page, Plantoir names the pages to look over before they go on your website.
  • If a change to several pages stops part way, the assistant says plainly that only part of it was made. On the Mac it also points you to Restore Section.
  • A deploy that has to rebuild a website made by a preview explains itself in plainer words.

Fixed

  • (Mac) Adding a section no longer shows a hidden page in the new section when that page's settings were written with quotation marks.
  • (Mac) Hiding or publishing a whole unit, publishing a class by its date, and the links checklist now change the right page when a class page shares its name with another page.
  • Class dates remembered with an impossible year are asked for again instead of being believed.

Plantoir 1.4.2

macOS only: Windows has no changes in this release; the Windows download is still 1.1.0.

New

  • Press Preview when today's class is published but the section's front page still shows an older one, and Plantoir offers to put today's class there. A "Not Today" button leaves things as they are.

Improved

  • Scheduling a deploy now names every place the course deploys to, and no longer warns about classes that are not published yet.
  • In the links checklist, a page that is only reached through another page is listed under it, and a page brought along by a ticked class is shown coming with it. Pages are named by their titles.
  • Asking the assistant (or Claude or Codex) which courses you have now names every place each one deploys to.
  • Setting up a course at the command line now follows the same course-code rules as the apps.

Fixed

  • The first colour scheme is now called "Standard Colours". Your courses keep the colours they already have.

Plantoir 1.4.1

macOS only: Windows has no changes in this release; the Windows download on plantoir.app is still 1.1.0.

This release is for the Mac. It makes previewing and deploying more dependable, tidies Course Settings, and adds a checklist for pages that link to pages students cannot see yet. Plantoir 1.4.0 will offer it to you by itself.

New

  • When a page you are publishing links to pages that are hidden, Plantoir shows a checklist in the section window. Tick the pages to publish, each dated like the class that uses it. A hidden class is offered unticked and brings its own pages along. Choosing Not Now publishes nothing.
  • With "This is a club" ticked, the New Course panel says Meetings, Club code, Club name and Create Club.

Improved

  • A preview that has to wait now says what it is waiting for.
  • A section cannot be previewed while that same section is being deployed, whether the deploy came from another window, the assistant or Terminal.
  • Get Ready for the Start of the Year names pages by their titles, and adds a folder only when two pages share a title.
  • Course Settings shows the Class Pages rows only for a course that recorded them, such as a club, and says "Language and region" instead of "Language / region (Quartz locale)".
  • Course Settings' Save button looks disabled when it is, and says why when something holds it back.
  • Every text field now has the same visible border.
  • The details shown under a preview, a deploy or a new course say "website builder", never container or Docker.

Fixed

  • Work left behind by a closed Revise with Claude or Codex session no longer stops previews until the Mac restarts.
  • A deploy you ask Claude or Codex for now stops at a question and tells you to deploy once from Plantoir, instead of waiting for ever.
  • An emoji or grade-in-title setting in Course Settings no longer changes on its own.
  • Copy a Page's checklist, and the screen after it, now fit on the screen however many pages are skipped.
  • The example course's progress bar now reaches every step.
  • Deploying to Cloudflare Pages after its project was deleted there now makes the project again instead of stopping.

Plantoir 1.4.0

This release is for the Mac. It is the biggest one since Plantoir began: Plantoir now keeps itself up to date, the first course on a new Mac starts much sooner, and there is new help for the start of the year, for clubs and for deploying on a schedule.

Before you update

  • This is the last release you install by hand. From 1.4.0 on, Plantoir checks for new versions by itself and asks you before installing one. If you are on 1.3.1 or earlier, download this one yourself; after that, you will not need to.
  • The Mac download is now about 411 MB (it used to be about 60 MB). Plantoir now carries its own copies of the helper programs it used to download the first time it ran, so the first course on a new Mac is ready much sooner. A download this much bigger than you remember is still the right file.
  • A deploy you scheduled before updating still happens as you set it. Until it runs it may appear under a slightly different name than new ones; it can be shown, cancelled and run just as before. Scheduling that section again replaces it.

New

  • Plantoir finds its own new versions, asks before installing them, and never installs one while it is building, previewing or deploying.
  • Get Ready for the Start of the Year… puts every class after the first into draft in one step. You see what will change first, and you can undo it.
  • This is a club in the New Course wizard: weekly meeting pages and a club front page, and the assistant talks about "meetings" rather than classes.
  • A How I Teach page for each course, which Claude and Codex read before helping with it. Open or create it from Course Settings.
  • A course with two curriculum folders gets a coverage map for each, and College Board codes count.
  • Ready-made example content for TAS2O.
  • A deploy set for later tells you how it went in a notification, even when Plantoir is closed. Clicking the notification opens that section.
  • The assistant can answer "What does Unit 2, Day 3 link to?" straight from the page, and "Publish all the classes in Unit 2." publishes the unit.
  • The build warns you when a published class links to pages students cannot see yet.

Improved

  • The first time Plantoir runs on a Mac, it gets the website builder ready in the background, and that first build is smaller and faster.
  • Plantoir reopens on the working folder you used last.
  • Every folder and file list in Course Settings and the New Course wizard is now a table with checkboxes.
  • The Backups list shows how much space each backup takes, and you can delete several at once.
  • The front page, and every page a class links to, show that class's date.
  • A scheduled deploy goes where the course deploys at the time it runs, and every deploy uses the settings as you last saved them.
  • The assistant reads a course's settings when it acts, not when its window was opened.
  • Times the assistant cannot place, such as "deploy at 6:30", are asked about instead of deploying right away. "Publish all of those" asks which pages you mean.
  • Duplicating a class that moves other classes warns you, on its card, that Undo will not move them back.
  • Two working folders that hold the same course each keep their own scheduled deploy.
  • A page whose settings Plantoir cannot read is hidden from students and named in the build, instead of being published or stopping the build.
  • Messages about a working folder say plainly what is wrong, and the first-run messages talk about "your website builder".
  • Clearer wording in several places: skeleton pages no longer show "{subject}", the skeleton choice says "an English skeleton", and the wizard's unit row no longer says "Unit" twice.

Fixed

  • Hide from the site's sidebar now always matches the built site, even with two windows open or a preview running.
  • Unpublishing a class no longer hides another class it links to.
  • Adding a section no longer publishes a page you had hidden.
  • Publishing now follows every way of writing a link — with an escaped |, in angle brackets, or Markdown style — and never follows a link inside code or a %% comment.
  • Pages with unusually written settings are no longer treated as hidden, broken by a restore, or skipped. Moving or renaming a class no longer leaves half a date behind.
  • A scheduled deploy whose build failed no longer names a destination it never reached.
  • A deploy to a folder lands where it says, or tells you it did not. Pressing Cancel during a deploy ends it quietly.
  • Previews: the address is never lost, a Mac that cannot reach the website builder stops within seconds instead of waiting, each working folder finds room for its own previews, and two people on one Mac no longer see each other's previews.
  • The window, the assistant, a scheduled deploy and an outside assistant can no longer build the same course at the same time.
  • A working folder whose name has an accent or different capitals no longer gets a second website builder.
  • Plantoir no longer offers to use a working folder that the website builder cannot reach.
  • Approving a change from the assistant no longer freezes the window while the course is backed up.
  • Copies and imports of a course no longer bring its Obsidian add-ons along.
  • One unreadable character no longer empties a problem report.
  • A course can no longer be called "work", and the folder path shown under a chosen folder now names every folder in it.
  • Four ready-made curriculum explainers no longer link to pages a skeleton course does not have.

  • A fill-in-the-blank question with one blank says "Not quite. Try again, or show the answer." when the answer is wrong, the same as a short-answer question. A question with two or more blanks where exactly one is right says "1 of 2 blanks is right. Try again, or show the answer."

New

Pasting several lines answers one question per line, and "No more input" ends the input.

Plantoir 1.4.0

This release is for the Mac. It is the biggest one since Plantoir began: Plantoir now keeps itself up to date, the first course on a new Mac starts much sooner, and there is new help for the start of the year, for clubs and for deploying on a schedule.

Before you update

  • This is the last release you install by hand. From 1.4.0 on, Plantoir checks for new versions by itself and asks you before installing one. If you are on 1.3.1 or earlier, download this one yourself; after that, you will not need to.
  • The Mac download is now about 411 MB (it used to be about 60 MB). Plantoir now carries its own copies of the helper programs it used to download the first time it ran, so the first course on a new Mac is ready much sooner. A download this much bigger than you remember is still the right file.
  • A deploy you scheduled before updating still happens as you set it. Until it runs it may appear under a slightly different name than new ones; it can be shown, cancelled and run just as before. Scheduling that section again replaces it.

New

  • Plantoir finds its own new versions, asks before installing them, and never installs one while it is building, previewing or deploying.
  • Get Ready for the Start of the Year… puts every class after the first into draft in one step. You see what will change first, and you can undo it.
  • This is a club in the New Course wizard: weekly meeting pages and a club front page, and the assistant talks about "meetings" rather than classes.
  • A How I Teach page for each course, which Claude and Codex read before helping with it. Open or create it from Course Settings.
  • A course with two curriculum folders gets a coverage map for each, and College Board codes count.
  • Ready-made example content for TAS2O.
  • A deploy set for later tells you how it went in a notification, even when Plantoir is closed. Clicking the notification opens that section.
  • The assistant can answer "What does Unit 2, Day 3 link to?" straight from the page, and "Publish all the classes in Unit 2." publishes the unit.
  • The build warns you when a published class links to pages students cannot see yet.
